sentence: Gabapentinoids are the group that contains pregabalin and gabapentin, which are used for epilepsy and nerve pain.
note: NHS pages: both used for epilepsy and nerve pain; gabapentinoids is the class name.

sentence: For epilepsy, these medicines are thought to reduce abnormal electrical activity in the brain.
note: NHS gabapentin/pregabalin summaries: reduce abnormal electrical activity.

sentence: For nerve pain, they are thought to block pain by affecting pain messages travelling through the brain and down the spine.
note: NHS summaries: block pain messages through brain and down spine.

sentence: The NHS lists drowsiness and dizziness among the common side effects of both medicines.
note: NHS: drowsiness and dizziness common (gabapentin side effects page; pregabalin sleepy/dizzy); addiction; gradual reduction.

sentence: The NHS says some people can become addicted to either medicine.
note: NHS: drowsiness and dizziness common (gabapentin side effects page; pregabalin sleepy/dizzy); addiction; gradual reduction.

sentence: The NHS says that when stopping either medicine the dose is reduced gradually to avoid withdrawal symptoms.
note: NHS: drowsiness and dizziness common (gabapentin side effects page; pregabalin sleepy/dizzy); addiction; gradual reduction.

sentence: The MHRA says gabapentin and pregabalin can cause potentially fatal respiratory depression, particularly when used with opioid medicines and alcohol.
Pregabalin and gabapentin became Class C controlled drugs, and Schedule 3 under the Misuse of Drugs Regulations 2001, on 1 April 2019.
note: GOV.UK news: Class C, Schedule 3 of the 2001 Regulations from 1 April 2019.

sentence: The MHRA reports severe breathing difficulty with pregabalin, and a separate update covers gabapentin.
note: MHRA pregabalin DSU and separate gabapentin DSU both returned.
